context.title: When an agent works for you at scale, approvals either interrupt you or stop the work
context.body: Aside can act across sites you're signed into, and it already has thoughtful controls: Guard mode, Queue and Steer, and sensitive actions like sending or paying wait for approval. But a task like 'send a personal note to 12 design leads' produces 12 sends to approve, and a single sign-in check or CAPTCHA stops the task until someone deals with it. The role asks for 'progress states, review, and recovery' for exactly this kind of work, including 'personalized outreach at scale'.
assumptions: I haven't used Aside. My view comes from two detailed public reviews and the job post, so the product may already do some of this.
aside.com didn't load for me, so the visuals follow macOS-native conventions and Aside's 'New York' sidebar layout as described publicly. No Aside logo.
Sending 'one by one, at a human pace' is a proposal, as is pausing only the blocked item.
People, companies and messages are fictional.

goals.title: Review once, not 12 times
goals.body: Sends collect in one lane you can scan, edit or skip.

goals.title: Keep working while you decide
goals.body: Research continues; only the send waits for you.

goals.title: Blocked, not stopped
goals.body: A sign-in check pauses one item, with a clear way to take over.

jtbd: When I hand Aside a batch of personal outreach, I want to approve what goes out in one calm pass, so I stay in control without babysitting the task.

evidence.finding: Sensitive actions such as payments, posting or sending wait for user approval; Guard is the default permission mode.

evidence.finding: MFA, CAPTCHA and identity checks stop the task until a person completes them; 'Take over' lets you continue an agent tab manually.

A Review lane that fills while the agent works

ranges.title: Approve each send
ranges.summary: A modal asks for approval each time the agent reaches a send.

ranges.title: Draft all, then review
ranges.summary: The agent drafts all 12 first, then shows one review list.
cons: Nothing goes out until the slowest one is done.

screens.alt: Sketch: batch review of all drafts

ranges.title: Review Lane
ranges.summary: Ready sends collect in a lane you can scan, edit or skip while research continues; blocks pause one item; a summary shows sent, skipped and needs-you.
pros: Recovery is per item, not per task.
cons: Needs care so batching doesn't feel like rubber-stamping.

screens.alt: Sketch: blocked item with take over
screens.label: Blocked

decision.title: Review Lane: approve in one pass, recover per item
decision.body: Range 3. Sends collect in a Review lane with the source each note used, while Aside keeps researching. A sign-in check pauses only the affected person, with 'Take over this tab'. The task ends with what was sent, skipped and still needs you.
reasons: It keeps the approval gate explicit, which matters most when an agent writes to other people.
Batching cuts interruptions without hiding what goes out.
Per-item recovery turns a stopped task into one small decision.
decision.tradeoff: Batch approval can turn into rubber-stamping. Showing the source behind each note, and expanding the first one by default, keeps the review real.

depth.body: Built in a macOS-native style with Aside's vertical sidebar (tabs, Agent Tabs, tasks). Three moments in an outreach task: four ready notes in the Review lane, each with what it was based on and a Skip, while research continues; a sign-in check that pauses only Tom's message, with Take over or Skip, and four sends already done; and a summary with sent, skipped and needs-you, plus updating the source sheet. Cards ease in, and motion turns off for people who reduce it.

validation.method: I'd look at how often outreach-style tasks are abandoned at an approval or a block, then test the lane with ten heavy users from the community.
hypotheses: Users approve sends in fewer sessions without editing less.
Fewer tasks are abandoned after a sign-in check.
Users trust Aside with larger batches over time.

metrics.name: Approval sessions per task
metrics.definition: Separate times a user returns to approve sends in one task.

metrics.name: Blocked-task completion
metrics.definition: Share of tasks hitting a block that still finish.

metrics.name: Edit rate
metrics.definition: Share of drafts edited before sending (watch for rubber-stamping).

nextSteps: Map every action type that waits for approval today.
Test the lane with ten community users on real outreach.
Define pacing rules per site with engineering.
Extend the pattern to payments and form submissions.
